How to clean up after a fire extinguisher according to luckyguy.

Ok. You just had a fire. You were quick acting and put out the fire with a liberal application of a fire extinguisher. Now let's get to clean up.

First is to identify the room with the greatest amount of fire retardent dry chemical. Our end game is removing this. Isolate the room from the rest of the house or business facility. Clean the entire premises out side of the target room of residue dust. This will allow you to continue operations / household living while targeting the main room and give us a clean staging area from which to clean it. To do this vaccume every area that has flooring or carpeting. Break down the remaining chemical with an appropriate complementary chemical. For sodium bicarbonate power a dilute solution of vinager, for monoamominum phosphate a solution of baking soda. Rinse clean by thorough mopping with extra water, then removing the water with a dry mop. Breaking down the powder will reduce partical size by a significant factor help it not clog up a mop quickly. Wipe down all surfaces.

This can be a long and tedious process but now that we have living and work space regained we can resume normal operations while we target the main room. You may have a thick dust several milimeters thick on all surfaces. The power is designed to get into every crevous and to stay aloft in the air as long as possible, hense why a fire extinguisher can manage to get a film of dust on the opposite end of a building. Remove a window and place a high power fan in the window. Seal off extra gaps with cardboard. Open a door to the room and turn the fan on with windows on the opposite side of the building open as well. We've essecially turned the room into a giant fume hood that we can work in. This will prevent any particle from passing the threshhold of the room and give you an enjoyable amount of ventilation while you work. With a shop vac clean each item in the room thoroughly before removing the item from the room. Be sure to keep the exaust of the shop vac pointed away from the open door if possible as it may kick up dust. Start first with the thick pool of powder on the floor then work your way from high to low. Now that everything has been vaccumed and removed wiped down the removed items and any furniture left in the room. This is a long process but you are now done and can enjoy life as normal.
